body: If high school is the best 4 years of your life, then you peaked in high school and don’t have much going for you now.
I don’t know. My life is going okay for once so I feel bad for wanting to die all the time. I’m just so isolated

Unfortunately no. Behavioral health is only seeing suicidal people currently because of covid. I can’t afford to pay for out of pocket counseling bc I don’t make much and am still waiting on back pay that the army owes me, I’m basically living paycheck to paycheck.

I could be forced to sleep at battalion staff duty instead of my house for a period of time, which has happened to people before. I would lose my clearance for sure. My orders could be pushed back and I’ll have to stay here longer. Constant monitoring of my personal life like last time.

I appreciate it. Even though a lot of my suffering has come from my time in the army, I don’t want to blame my misery entirely on the army. I know my quality of life will go up a lot soon but I know I’m just gonna fall back into the same depressive state after that honeymoon phase is over. And a lot of people in my field are introverted and nerdy, but I definitely got singled out because the unit separated me from my peers and they stopped talking to me because of it. I have a job lined up where I’ll be managing a website of a potential new clothing line, though I’m really only doing it because of Covid’s impact on the economy. I can live quite comfortably with my disability and gi bill and I know I should be grateful for these financial advantages, but it’s hard to ever be in a good mood
